title: Revocation and the past; the new enemy
objective: State revocation as two temporal statements, show that one holds on single-copy traces and that a short trace refutes the other, and show a stale-replica read after an ACL change.

choice.prompt: Restate CL-6.3 from memory. A read after an ACL change is served from a lagging replica. Which part of CL-6.3's card cracks?

options.why: Every checked history is still accepted.
The implementation never left the model. The model assumed something.
It is SEAM-9's clause, "nothing reads a replica".

choice.prompt: Birch revokes dana's access to contract, which she opened last week. What does revocation guarantee?

options.text: She loses access, and she loses what she already saw.
Her later opens fail if the check reads an up-to-date ACL, and what she already received stays known.
options.why: Revocation governs the future, through the ACL the check reads.

options.text: Her later opens fail at once, whatever copy of the ACL the check reads.
options.why: A stale copy still says yes.

blocks.md: Revocation can promise two different things, and both are temporal statements, written as in S5. **S-new** says that after revocation no new read succeeds: `□[ReadOK(u, d) ⇒ canread(u, d)]_vars`, a safety property. **S-past** says that revocation removes what was already read: `□[Revoke(u, d) ⇒ d ∉ delivered′[u]]_vars`.
The interpreter replays one trace on a single-copy model, where `Open` checks the current ACL, and evaluates both statements over it. `delivered[u]` is the log of every page returned to u.
blocks.direction: Trace asserts: a share, a read, a revocation and a second read. Each statement is judged over the behavior this trace produces.

code.text:
trace
  Share(contract -> dana)
  Open(dana, contract)
  Revoke(dana, contract)
  Open(dana, contract)

S-new   □[ReadOK(u, d) ⇒ canread(u, d)]_vars
S-past  □[Revoke(u, d) ⇒ d ∉ delivered′[u]]_vars

call.prompt: Is S-past refuted on this trace?

options.why: After `Revoke`, dana's delivered log still holds the page.
Revocation stops future reads only, and the statement asks for more.

blocks.after: The second `Open` is refused, so S-new holds on this trace, and dana's delivered log still holds the page after `Revoke`, so S-past is refuted {{run:RUN-interp-revocation}}. This is SP-7.3. Knowledge only grows, `□(d ∈ delivered[u] ⇒ □(d ∈ delivered[u]))`, so revocation can govern the future and nothing else. For the past, the release record's "when" says what holds: delivered stays delivered.

blocks.md: Zanzibar's paper gives the new enemy: "Bob should not be able to see the new contents, but may do so if the ACL check is evaluated with a stale ACL from before Bob's removal" (§2.2). Here `Open` checks the ACL on a lagging replica and reads content from the primary.
`Sync` copies the primary's ACL to the replica. gia revokes dana and edits contract on the primary, and dana opens contract.
blocks.direction: Trace asserts: the replica last synced before the revocation, then one edit on the primary and one read by dana.

code.text:
trace
  Share(contract -> dana)
  Sync
  Revoke(dana, contract)
  Edit(contract, body = "v2")
  Open(dana, contract)

Open(u, d)  checks the ACL on the replica, reads the content from the primary

options.why: The check consulted a copy that had not heard of the revocation.
A stale ACL was applied to new content.
The ACL and the content come from different copies here.

blocks.after: S-new fails on the replicated model {{run:RUN-interp-new-enemy}}. This is SP-7.6, and it is an erosion: CL-6.3's assumption that nothing reads a replica cracks, while CL-6.2 does not rest on that clause and stands. Three remedies: check the ACL and read the content at one snapshot; keep a consistency token with each content version and require an ACL snapshot at least as fresh; or route reads after an ACL change to the primary. The claim records the choice as [E] where it is enforced and as [A] otherwise.

choice.prompt: On the replicated model, where `Open` checks the replica and `Sync` copies the primary's ACL to it, which trace violates S-new?

options.why: No read follows the revocation. This trace breaks S-past, not S-new.
The replica still lists dana, so the read succeeds after the revocation.

options.text: None: the check reads an ACL, so no read after a revocation succeeds.
options.why: The ACL it reads may be a stale copy.

choice.prompt: Which statement holds for a system whose ACL check reads a replica?

options.text: Once `Revoke` returns, no later read by that user succeeds.
options.why: A read can succeed until the replica hears of the revocation.

options.text: Whatever the user read before the revocation is erased.
A later read can succeed until the replica hears of the revocation, and what was already read stays known.
options.why: Both halves follow from the model: the check reads a copy, and knowledge only grows.

blocks.title: Build this
blocks.md: In LAB-7.6, state S-new as a monitor that accepts fresh single-copy traces, and let your S-past monitor reject a trace the interpreter replays.

blocks.title: Twin
blocks.md: Zanzibar, Google's authorization system, met this problem. It stores a consistency token, a zookie, with each content version, and evaluates the ACL check at a snapshot at least as fresh as that token (§2.2, read 2026-10-23). The paper describes a closed system, so there is no commit to pin.

blocks.title: Reading
blocks.md: [Zanzibar](https://www.usenix.org/conference/atc19/presentation/pang), §2.2 "Consistency Model", pp. 34 to 35 (read 2026-10-23). Sibling course: byzantine's consistency material treats the same new enemy as an ordering problem, and drawer D-21 is its one-page prerequisite.

RUN-interp-new-enemy.title: INS-interp on S7.L8 cell 2: gia revokes dana, edits contract's body, and dana opens contract; on one copy the open is refused, and with the ACL check on a replica 2 steps behind the primary dana receives the new body, refuting S-new
verdict_lines: trace commands.txt on W0, replicated model, ACL replica 2 steps behind the primary
1. Revoke(gia: contract -> dana); canread no; delivered []
2. Edit(gia: contract.body = "the body after the revocation"); canread yes; delivered []
3. Open(dana, contract) -> contract@2 "the body after the revocation"; canread no; delivered [contract@2]
S-new (after revocation, no new read succeeds): refuted at step 3
S-past (revocation removes what was already read): holds
notes: The replica lag is a model parameter [D]: the new enemy needs the ACL check to read a copy older than the revocation.
The S7 interpreter has no Lean reference (tracker W4-T27).

RUN-interp-revocation.title: INS-interp on S7.L8 cell 1, single copy: Share, Open, Revoke, Open on contract for dana; S-new holds, and S-past is refuted at the Revoke step because the page delivered before it stays in dana's log
verdict_lines: trace commands.txt on W0, single copy
1. Share(gia: contract -> dana); canread yes; delivered []
2. Open(dana, contract) -> contract@1 "contract body"; canread yes; delivered [contract@1]
3. Revoke(gia: contract -> dana); canread no; delivered [contract@1]
4. Open(dana, contract) -> refused; canread no; delivered [contract@1]
S-new (after revocation, no new read succeeds): holds
S-past (revocation removes what was already read): refuted at step 3: contract@1 is still delivered

single-copy.s_past: refuted at step 3: contract@1 is still delivered

notes: A trace step records the state right after its command; delivered is the subject's log of pages, which only grows.
The S7 interpreter has no Lean reference (tracker W4-T27).
